text:
Everything about Colorado's season changed in 57 seconds in Ottawa. Daily Faceoff reported that Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar both left Thursday's game with lower-body injuries, and no timeline has been given. The Avs clawed back from 2-0 down, took the lead and lost in overtime on what Corey Masisak of the Denver Post called "a weird, wild night".

Before that night, Colorado is 11-6-3 with 25 points, owns 55.2% of the expected goals and scores 4.05 goals a game. Our playoff race has them at 96%. The MacKinnon line with Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas has outscored opponents 20-10 at 5-on-5, and Makar with Devon Toews takes 60% of the expected goals. Those are the two engines, and both are now in question.

There's some cushion. The Avalanche have scored 12.8 more goals than their chances predicted, and the Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal noted the power play is running at 26.8% since assistant Brett McLean took it over. Toews has 12 points in 10 games on 6.8 expected, and he'll be asked for more. Nazem Kadri, Brock Nelson and Gabriel Landeskog give Jared Bednar real depth.

The worry is the crease. Scott Wedgewood is .882 over his last five starts, 4.4 goals worse than expected. Without the two stars, the goaltending has far less room to be ordinary. Watch the injury news first.
headline: The Avalanche wait on MacKinnon and Makar
